# Question answer — generator-shortcuts

## Strongest plausible shortcut

The strongest measured rival after the first repair was:

> Red (`2`) sources emit orange (`7`) cardinal rays. Rays stop at other red sources and at color `8`, but pass through every other nonzero color. Preserve all input nonzero cells.

This is `single_blocker_color_only` in the repaired module.

It fits all four canonical pairs because canonical inputs contain only `0` and `2`; no example contains an obstacle color that can distinguish “stop at every nonzero” from “stop only at red and 8.” It also fit every first-round generated sample because that generator used only color `8` as a blocker: `600/600` easy, `600/600` medium, and `600/600` hard.

A second important canonical-fitting shortcut is `dedupe_shared_axis`: retain only the first source from any already-used row or column. Canonical sources have distinct rows and columns, so this also fits `4/4` public pairs. It survived `360/2,160` first-round demo windows and changed the next aligned-source query in all 360.

## Exact disagreement input

Version `4.0.0` emits the following input for seed `91`, sample index `1`, difficulty `medium`, and overrides `grid_h=7`, `grid_w=10`, `seed_count=3`, `scene_kind="blocked"`:

```text
0000000000
0000000000
0000000000
0203000000
0000000020
0000000000
0208000000
```

The blockers are color `3` at zero-indexed `(3,3)` and color `8` at `(6,3)`. Each is independently observable.

The intended output is:

```text
0700000070
0700000070
0700000070
7273000070
7777777727
0700000070
7278000070
```

The color-8-only rival passes through the color-`3` blocker and produces:

```text
0700000070
0700000070
0700000070
7273777777
7777777727
0700000070
7278000070
```

It disagrees at five cells in row 3: columns `4`, `5`, `6`, `7`, and `9`, where the intended answer remains `0` and the rival paints `7`.

The same exact probe also distinguishes three other canonical-fitting shortcuts:

| Shortcut | Differing cells |
|---|---:|
| paint through every nonzero | 10 |
| every nonzero cell emits | 14 |
| deduplicate shared-axis sources | 2 |

## How the output was checked

I evaluated the exact input with the pinned canonical Racket `program_solution`, not only by hand or with the Python mirror. The Racket output equals `rule_mirror` exactly. The replay contains the input, authority hash, blockers, Racket output, mirror output, all four rival outputs, and every differing coordinate:

`checks/round2-after/exact-two-color-witness.json`

Broader independent checks agree:

- Racket smoke: `120/120` generated inputs matched the mirror, with zero crashes;
- semantic gate: all four canonical-fitting shortcuts were confirmed against `4/4` public pairs and refuted by generated witnesses;
- deep audit: zero of 12 competitors survived any of 216 sliding three-demo windows;
- blocker audit: all `216/216` sampled probes had two distinct independently observable blockers.

## Does the proposed generator emit such cases?

Yes. `two_color_blocker_probe` is one slot of the period-three default schedule, so every three consecutive examples contains exactly one such counterexample. It always contains color `8` plus a different blocker color selected from `{1,3,4,5,6,9}`. The second-round semantic census generated the profile `223/600` times across all bands, and the task-local deep audit found no surviving named shortcut in any tested window.
